details.alignment: Lawful Neutral — Loyalist reading; Waluigi files her as zealot

biography.value:
Captain Toadette — the Ruthless Restorer. Military commander of the Peach Loyalists. Waluigi's dossier calls her the scariest person in the Mushroom Kingdom who is not a dimensional horror. She plans operations with patience and executes them with total commitment.

Status: Active — commanding Peach Loyalist forces.

Affiliation: Peach Loyalists.

Table build: Level 3 Circle of the Land (Forest) Druid. This is a rules translation of her siege work at Bramblehaven — sappers, simultaneous breaches, earth and thorn used as military tools — not a claim that the lore file named a D&D class. The player asked for Druid. Wild Shape and land-circle spells stand in for fieldcraft and the no-retreat earthworks.

Canon warning: She shot a sergeant for suggesting retreat. After Bramblehaven fell, fifteen surrendering garrison troops were executed under her standing no-quarter order. Peach would not have approved. The sheet does not award extra XP for that. File new XP in the ledger first.

Inventory policy: command staff, hide, shield, field kit, Loyalist orders, and one witness card for the Fall of Bramblehaven. No shop relics, no balcony-rail fragments, no bootleg fans.

details.appearance: A compact, hardy Toad carrying an axe too large for anyone who has not watched him use it. Scarred by flight, imprisonment, and the work of keeping frightened people alive.
details.trait: Total commitment. No retreats. Plans like a siege engineer.
details.ideal: Peach's memory is the only law that matters.
details.bond: The Peach Loyalists, and a princess who cannot talk back.
details.flaw: She will execute a surrender and call it justice. She shot her own sergeant for suggesting a tactical retreat.
details.eyes: Two ordinary eyes and one Feyward sensory eye
details.faith: Unresolved; has encountered forces that call themselves gods
details.skin: Toad green with Feywild color shift

armorProf.custom: Light, medium, and heavy armor; shields. Dan fights one-handed and does not receive a second-weapon benefit.

weaponProf.custom: Simple and martial weapons; longsword; one-handed use only.

biography.value:
Feyward Dan — Player Character Dossier

Level 3 One-Armed Feyward Paladin / Dimensional Escapee. This is the parallel Feyward Dan, not the original Dan who led the Liberated Toads and lost his arm to the corrupted mage staff. Feyward Dan woke in a yellow bed at Prismari's school, survived goblin betrayal, escaped through a window, was dragged through the Mazebound, slept through multiple dimensional emergencies, and opened his third sensory eye during the Imp Ambush.

Ledger: 1,960 XP, 11 entries, Level 3, Power 5 Mortal. The actor is a playable translation of the lore; the XP ledger remains authoritative.

Confirmed carried inventory: one sword of uncertain provenance, chain mail, Shield +1, Holy Symbol of Ravenkind, and ten gold pieces. The sword is the blade Dan used when he charged Professor Prismari after the explosion on Estragon's Island. The school journal, Prismari, Mazebound, and other events remain in the biography and source records rather than being invented as carried loot.

Inventory rule: this actor deliberately contains only gear and abilities Dan actually has or was explicitly assigned. Memories, event records, and things he merely saw are not added to the inventory as fake loot.

How to play Feyward Dan

Use charm, improvisation, and sensory magic before force. Dan is not a polished wizard. He is a displaced player character who survives by testing doors, apologizing, fleeing when necessary, and returning when the party needs his eye.

One-armed paladin rules

Dan uses a longsword in his remaining hand and a shield in the other available hand. He cannot dual-wield or make two-handed weapon attacks. Divine Sense, Divine Smite, and the Aura of Life campaign item are included as documents. Aura of Life is recorded as a story/boon item and should be level-gated by the GM if standard 5e progression is being enforced.
biography.public: Feyward Dan is a parallel Toad with a colorful Feywild aura, an unreliable itinerary, and one extra eye that sees what invisible enemies hoped would remain unseen.

items.name: Druid — Circle of the Land (Forest), Level 3

description.value: Level 3 Druid. Circle of the Land — Forest. Spellcasting Wisdom. Hit die d8. A table translation of Toadette's siege-and-restoration command style.
Toad. Small. Walk 25 ft. The sports-and-party Toadette Waluigi remembers is not the one on this sheet. This one commands a crusade.
Background: military command of the Peach Loyalists. Fall of Bramblehaven — overnight sappers, three simultaneous breaches, a bastion taken in a day. Then the courtyard.
You know Druidic. You leave marks only another druid (or a very determined auditor) can read. Toadette uses it for sapper signs and no-retreat route marks.

Twice per short rest, bonus action, assume a beast form (CR 1/4, no fly/swim at this level unless the GM allows campaign beasts). Used here as fieldcraft and sapper cover, not as a joke mushroom mascot.

Land's Aid / Natural Recovery flavor: after a short rest, recover spell slots totaling half Druid level (rounded up). Circle spells (always prepared): barkskin, spider climb, spike growth, pass without trace — filed as siege tools (cover, walls, caltrops of thorn, silent approach).

Campaign feature — GM review. Toadette's written order: no prisoners from Fawful's forces. This is not a damage bonus. It is a political and moral fact on the sheet so the table cannot pretend it is not there. Using it has consequences. Peach would not have signed it.

Advantage on Intelligence (History) or Wisdom (Survival) checks to plan a breach, place sappers, or time three simultaneous attacks. Does not grant extra attacks. The masterpiece is in the plan, not in a feat tax.

Reference card only. Does not award XP. The bastion fell in a day. Fifteen surrendering troops were executed in the keep courtyard under standing orders. Some Loyalists hesitated. They were overruled.
Toadette's field staff. Simple melee, 1d6 bludgeoning, versatile 1d8. Cast shillelagh to make it a Wisdom weapon (1d8 magical bludgeoning) for one minute.
Backup blade. 1d4 piercing, finesse, light, thrown 20/60. Not a relic.
Field hide. AC 12 + Dex (max 2). What a commander wears in a sapper trench, not a parade.
+2 AC. Peach's crown painted on the boss. The paint is newer than the grief.
10 uses. Stabilize a creature without a Medicine check.
Five days. The crusade still eats.
Breach timing. Three notes, three teams.
Paper, not magic. The no-quarter clause is written in her hand. Waluigi has the moral objection; the table has the exhibit.
Ordinary Mushroom Kingdom field fungus. 2d4+2 HP if the table treats it as a potion of healing. One dose. Not a shop gag item.
Druidic + military. Routes, charges, and the line that must not be crossed backward.
Water. Even crusades need it.
For goodberry adjuncts and field dressings. Wisdom tool.
Cantrip. Prestidigitation for plants. Weather tell, bloom, faint sensory mark.
